Prompt Engineering & The CO-STAR Framework

Master the foundational art of prompt design. Discover how structured prompt engineering turns vague, generic AI answers into precise, production-ready outputs.

Prompt Engineering Fundamentals

What is an AI Prompt?

A prompt is the natural language instruction, question, or scenario you provide to a Large Language Model (LLM) like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or DeepSeek. It functions as executable code in human syntax, directing the model's neural network to retrieve, reason, and generate the desired output.

The Golden Rule of Prompting

"Garbage in, garbage out. Precision in, brilliance out." LLMs are probabilistic prediction engines. When prompts lack constraints or context, the AI falls back on generic clichés or hallucinations. Specific boundaries unlock state-of-the-art results.

Why Use a Structured Framework?

Without a structured model, people frequently omit critical parameters: tone, target audience, format constraints, or situational context. Frameworks provide a reliable, repeatable mental model that guarantees consistent, enterprise-grade output every single time.

Created by Sheila Teo • Data Scientist (Singapore GPT-4 Competition Champion)
Official References: GovTech Singapore [1] YouTube [2] Portkey.ai [1] Parloa [2]

The CO-STAR prompting framework is a structured method designed to help you write clear, precise instructions for large language models to get high-quality and relevant outputs. Originally developed by data scientist Sheila Teo, the acronym stands for six key elements:

C
Context Background & Setting

Provide background information so the AI understands the specific scenario, industry, company situation, or environment it operates in.

Example: "I am a B2B SaaS founder launching an AI marketing analytics platform for mid-market retail agencies."
O
Objective Task & Mission

Clearly define the task or what you want the AI to achieve. Give the model a singular, laser-focused deliverable.

Example: "Write a high-converting 3-part cold email sequence designed to get readers to book a 15-minute product demo."
S
Style Writing Style & Format

Specify the writing or communication format/style (e.g., bullet points, a professional report, short punchy sentences, or mimicking an expert like Ogilvy).

Example: "Style of David Ogilvy: punchy opening hook, concise bullet points for benefits, short sentences, zero corporate jargon."
T
Tone Emotional Attitude

Set the emotional character or attitude of the response (e.g., professional, friendly, persuasive, empathetic, or reassuring).

Example: "Persuasive, authoritative yet warmly approachable and respectful of their busy schedule."
A
Audience Target Reader

Identify who will read or use the output so the language, technical depth, and vocabulary match their level.

Example: "Time-starved Chief Marketing Officers (CMOs) who manage teams of 15+ and care about ROI and CAC reduction."
R
Response Format & Structure

Define the final format, length, or structure of the output (e.g., a 200-word text, markdown table, or a JSON file).

Example: "Provide 3 emails. Each under 120 words. Format with: Subject Line, Preview Text, Body, and 1 Clear CTA button."
CO-STAR in Action: Before vs. After
Without Framework (Vague Prompt)

"Write me a cold email to sell my AI tool to marketing managers."

Result: Generic 400-word corporate fluff with buzzwords like "revolutionize" and "leverage" that gets deleted instantly.
With CO-STAR (Engineered Prompt)
# CONTEXT: B2B SaaS founder launching AI marketing analytics for retail.
# OBJECTIVE: 3-part cold email sequence to book a 15-min discovery call.
# STYLE: David Ogilvy style: short hook, bulleted perks, zero fluff.
# TONE: Persuasive, authoritative yet empathetic to their busy day.
# AUDIENCE: CMOs of retail brands managing $2M+ ad budgets.
# RESPONSE: 3 emails, max 100 words each, with high-converting CTA.
Result: Laser-focused, highly relevant copy ready to deploy with maximum response rates.
Universal CO-STAR Prompt Template (Copy & Fill In)
